title: Making the Mr. Bear sides with an all-star band for Groove
summary: Rolontz needed rhythm and blues artists; McRae gathered Mickey Baker and others, who were surprised he was the artist.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x:
Yeah.
Anyway, what we did, Bob Rolontz -- only he had Piano Red out of Chicago. See, he had a hard time getting artists because he didn't know too much about rhythm and blues.
See, he took that job because RCA Victor wanted some of this rock and roll stuff. But they wanted to put it on RCA's label.
What they did, they created another label called Groove Records, so they brought in this rhythm and blues stuff.
So when I walked in, "Mr. Bear" "Peel-A-Bos" (inaudible) doing all this stuff with them, you know. Keep my good eye on you and all this stuff. Teacho and all them guys with me.
So I got this all star band. I got Mickey Baker and all these -- people come down with me -- all these stars, you know.
And the guys say, "Who's the artist?" Mickey Baker say, "Who's singing today? Teddy, who are you recording?" I say, "Me, I'm recording me."
